    orca: test probes run with no display; an explicit platform has a value

    lifetime case would each start a real GUI that `timeout` cannot reach
    past bwrap; both now run without WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY, so such a
    launch exits at Orca's display gate instead of opening a window.

    is what Orca's display gate reads, and a bare `--ozone-platform x11`
    gives Chromium an empty value, which the gate turns into X11.
    
    The PATH comment was backwards: env.nix puts the profile first by
    design (an Orca-sandboxed shell is the exception), so were the screen
    reader installed, `orca` would still be this CLI.
    
    Tests: the argv harness ignores the caller's ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE,
    refuses a wrapper with a second exec of the launcher, and falls back
    when there is no nixGL layer; the lifetime case's parent stays up 4s,
    for margin on a cold start, and still goes red with dieWithParent on.

commit 63f565ebc6eafb0436fa98fe0815480688a7ade9
Author: Sauyon Lee <git@sjle.co>
Date:   Sat Oct 24 12:58:41 2026 +0000

    orca: CLI on plain node as `orca-ide`/`orca`, six agent skills; GUI is `orca-ide-app`
    
    Install Orca's CLI the way upstream's .deb lays it out: `orca-ide` on
    PATH is the CLI, and the GUI is off that name (here `orca-ide-app`, used
    by the desktop Exec). Orca's skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal
    to run exactly `orca-ide`; master had the GUI there, with an always-on
    --ozone-platform=wayland that broke the GUI binary's own CLI dispatch
    ("Unknown flag --ozone-platform for command: open").
    
    The CLI is plain JavaScript, so it runs on nixpkgs' nodejs_24 (Electron
    43 bundles node 24) as a plain exec -- no sandbox between the caller and
    the CLI. ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE points `orca-ide open` at the nixGL-wrapped
    GUI; NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as upstream's shim does.
    
    GUI: the wayland flag only outside node mode (`serve` probes the GUI
    with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and Node rejects it); dieWithParent off,
    since the GUI that `open` spawns is the CLI's direct child.
    
    Six skills (orca-cli, orchestration, computer-use, orca-per-workspace-env,
    orca-linear, linear-tickets) from stablyai/orca at the AppImage's own
    sourceCommit; tests/orca-cli-skills.sh holds them to the hashes in the
    build's current-manifest.json and the rev to the sourceCommit.
    
    Supersedes the orca-cli-skills branch, which ran the CLI inside bwrap
    and needed a hand-written signal forwarder to stop `serve` cleanly.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: b23d9d602679

You are a file search specialist for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. You excel at thoroughly navigating and exploring codebases.

=== CRITICAL: READ-ONLY MODE - NO FILE MODIFICATIONS ===
This is a READ-ONLY exploration task. You are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from:
- Creating new files (no Write, touch, or file creation of any kind)
- Modifying existing files (no Edit operations)
- Deleting files (no rm or deletion)
- Moving or copying files (no mv or cp)
- Creating temporary files anywhere, including /tmp
- Using redirect operators (>, >>, |) or heredocs to write to files
- Running ANY commands that change system state

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

Your strengths:
- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns
- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

Guidelines:
- Use `find` via Bash for broad file pattern matching
- Use `grep` via Bash for searching file contents with regex
- Use Read when you know the specific file path you need to read
- Use Bash ONLY for read-only operations (ls, git status, git log, git diff, find, grep, cat, head, tail)
- NEVER use Bash for: mkdir, touch, rm, cp, mv, git add, git commit, npm install, pip install, or any file creation/modification
- Adapt your search approach based on the thoroughness level specified by the caller
- Communicate your final report directly as a regular message - do NOT attempt to create files

NOTE: You are meant to be a fast agent that returns output as quickly as possible. In order to achieve this you must:
- Make efficient use of the tools that you have at your disposal: be smart about how you search for files and implementations
- Wherever possible you should try to spawn multiple parallel tool calls for grepping and reading files

Complete the user's search request efficiently and report your findings clearly.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

diff --git a/orca.nix b/orca.nix
index ffeef930..342d26f1 100644
--- a/orca.nix
+++ b/orca.nix
@@ -32,10 +32,16 @@ let
     # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
     # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
     extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
-    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
-    # installs the CLI as `orca-ide`, and that is what the desktop Exec and
-    # meta.mainProgram use below. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin
-    # name, so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
+    # `orca-ide open` (orcaCli below) spawns the GUI detached, but every
+    # wrapper layer execs the next, so this bwrap is the CLI's own child, and
+    # --die-with-parent SIGKILLs the window the moment `open` returns.
+    dieWithParent = false;
+    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop. Upstream's .deb
+    # puts the CLI on PATH as `orca-ide` and leaves the GUI off it, and Orca's
+    # skills tell agents to run `orca-ide` outside an Orca terminal -- so
+    # `orca-ide` is orcaCli below, and the GUI is `orca-ide-app`, which the
+    # desktop Exec and meta.mainProgram use. Written by hand, not with
+    # makeShellWrapper: --add-flags cannot make the flag below conditional.
     #
     # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
     # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
@@ -43,21 +49,37 @@ let
     # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
     # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
     # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
-    # is a flag on the command line.
+    # is a flag on the command line -- except in node mode: the CLI's `serve`
+    # probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as
+    # argv, and Node rejects the flag ("bad option", exit 9). Nor when the
+    # caller sets a platform itself (Electron serve appends
+    # --ozone-platform=x11): `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`, which
+    # is what Orca's display gate reads -- a bare `--ozone-platform x11` gives
+    # Chromium an empty value, and a -hint is only a preference. (The flag
+    # also counts as explicit to Orca's own serve-mode X11 restart, so a
+    # hand-run `orca-ide-app --serve` stays on wayland; the CLI's serve
+    # passes x11 itself.)
     #
     # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
     # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
-    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bin/orca symlink from buildCommand
-    # is replaced with a wrapper that prepends the flag and passes "$@"
-    # through. buildFHSEnv's builder has no makeWrapper on PATH, so its setup
-    # hook is sourced by hand; and the wrapper must not target its own path
-    # (renaming to orca-ide and wrapping orca-ide in place makes it exec
-    # itself), so the bwrap launcher moves aside to .orca-ide-unwrapped.
+    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher's bin/orca moves aside
+    # to .orca-ide-unwrapped -- `orca` is orcaCli's name in the profile, and
+    # tests/sandbox-fonts.sh finds the launcher by this one -- and
+    # orca-ide-app execs it, the flag first when due.
     extraInstallCommands = ''
-      source ${pkgs.makeWrapper}/nix-support/setup-hook
       mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
-      makeShellWrapper $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped $out/bin/orca-ide \
-        --add-flags '--ozone-platform=wayland'
+      cat > $out/bin/orca-ide-app <<'EOF'
+      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
+      explicit=
+      for a in "$@"; do
+        case $a in --) break ;; --ozone-platform=?*) explicit=1; break ;; esac
+      done
+      if [ -z "$explicit" ] && [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then
+        set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"
+      fi
+      exec ${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped "$@"
+      EOF
+      chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide-app
       install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
         $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
       for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
@@ -66,9 +88,9 @@ let
           $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
       done
       substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
-        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
+        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide-app'
     '';
-    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
+    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide-app";
   };
   # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
   # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
@@ -90,6 +112,75 @@ let
   # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
   appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
 
+  # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
+  # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
+  # same reason parsec gets it.
+  orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;
+
+  # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
+  # Linux) and `orca`. Upstream avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it is
+  # usually the GNOME screen reader; it is not installed here, so `orca` is
+  # the CLI too. (Were it installed, the profile comes first on PATH --
+  # env.nix -- so `orca` would still be this CLI.) The skills say `orca-ide`.
+  #
+  # It is plain JavaScript: upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide runs it on the
+  # bundled Electron in node mode, but nothing in it needs Electron, so it
+  # runs on nixpkgs' node of the same major (Electron 43 bundles node 24)
+  # with no sandbox -- a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's
+  # own. Orca's own installer puts a shim dir on PATH only in Orca
+  # terminals, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path that goes
+  # stale on the next bump.
+  #
+  # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: the Orca binary for `orca-ide open` and `serve` to
+  # launch; under plain node there is no other, and without it `open` fails
+  # and `serve` refuses to start. NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as
+  # ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS and cleared, as upstream's shim does.
+  # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
+  orcaCli = pkgs.runCommand "orca-cli-${version}" {
+    pname = "orca-cli";
+    inherit version;
+    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
+  } ''
+    mkdir -p $out/bin
+    cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
+    #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
+    export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE="''${ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app}"
+    export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="''${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
+    export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="''${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
+    unset NODE_OPTIONS NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE
+    exec ${pkgs.nodejs_24}/bin/node ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js "$@"
+    EOF
+    chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide
+    ln -s orca-ide $out/bin/orca
+  '';
+
+  # Orca's agent skills, from the repo at the commit this AppImage was built
+  # from: `orca skills install` pins `npx skills add` to it, and the bundled
+  # resources/skills/current-manifest.json holds their sha256s. Bump this rev
+  # with the version — it is the `sourceCommit` in out/main/index.js of
+  # app.asar, and the test holds it to that. A fetch in this module rather
+  # than a flake input, because the rev tracks `version` above, not the
+  # repo's head; `nix flake update` does not touch it. The rev is in the
+  # store name so a rev bump without a hash bump fails to fetch instead of

@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done

+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+

+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.

+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
+

+# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).
+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too,
+# minus nixGL.

+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi

+# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=

+# it), except in node mode or when the caller sets a platform itself --
+# `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`. A bare `--ozone-platform x11`
+# does not count: Chromium takes no switch value from the next word, so
+# Orca's display gate sees an empty one and falls back to X11; nor does a
+# -hint, which the gate ignores.

+  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }

+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
+         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do

+  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi

+else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi

+# And for real: the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
+# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
+# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
+# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
+# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits at Orca's gate instead.
+nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"
+node_ok=
+if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
+  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
+# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
+# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
+# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
+# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
+if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
+  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
+else
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
+fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
+# completion too.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

index 00000000..6c3580d6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# No sandbox between the caller and the CLI: a plain exec of node, so
+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.
+if grep -q 'exec .*/bin/node ' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" && ! grep -q bwrap "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
+
+# Under plain node, `orca-ide open` has no Orca binary to spawn but
+# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).
+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too,
+# minus nixGL.
+app=$(sed -nE 's|.*ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-([^}]*)\}.*|\1|p' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")
+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# The GUI wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with its
+# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
+# wayland first (Hyprland has no X server, and Orca's gate picks X11 without
+# it), except in node mode or when the caller sets a platform itself --
+# `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`. A bare `--ozone-platform x11`
+# does not count: Chromium takes no switch value from the next word, so
+# Orca's display gate sees an empty one and falls back to X11; nor does a
+# -hint, which the gate ignores.
+inner=$(grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*/bin/orca-ide-app' "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" | tail -1)
+[ -n "$inner" ] || inner="$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"  # no nixGL layer
+sed -E 's|^exec .*/\.orca-ide-unwrapped "\$@"$|printf "%s\\n" "$@"|' "$inner" > "$T/argv"
+grep -q '^printf' "$T/argv" && ! grep -q 'orca-ide-unwrapped' "$T/argv" \
+  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }
+argv() { env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE bash "$T/argv" "$@" | paste -sd' '; }
+for c in "open|--ozone-platform=wayland open" \
+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
+         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do
+  in=${c%%|*}; want=${c#*|}
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+  got=$(argv $in)
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "GUI argv: '$in' -> '$want'"
+  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi
+done
+got=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 bash "$T/argv" -e 1 | paste -sd' ')
+if [ "$got" = "-e 1" ]; then pass "GUI argv: node mode gets no flag"
+else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi
+
+# And for real: the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
+# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
+# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
+# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
+# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits at Orca's gate instead.
+nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"
+node_ok=
+if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
+  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
+# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
+# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
+# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
+# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
+if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
+  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
+else
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
+fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
+# completion too.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

    99	  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
   100	  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
   101	  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
   102	  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
   103	    <?xml version="1.0"?>
   104	    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
   105	    <fontconfig>
   106	      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
   107	      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
   108	      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
   109	    </fontconfig>
   110	  '';
   111	  # Extracted once, shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below;
   112	  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
   113	  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
   114	
   115	  # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
   116	  # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
   117	  # same reason parsec gets it.
   118	  orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;
   119	
   120	  # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
   121	  # Linux) and `orca`. Upstream avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it is
   122	  # usually the GNOME screen reader; it is not installed here, so `orca` is
   123	  # the CLI too. (Were it installed, the profile comes first on PATH --
   124	  # env.nix -- so `orca` would still be this CLI.) The skills say `orca-ide`.
   125	  #
   126	  # It is plain JavaScript: upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide runs it on the
   127	  # bundled Electron in node mode, but nothing in it needs Electron, so it
   128	  # runs on nixpkgs' node of the same major (Electron 43 bundles node 24)
   129	  # with no sandbox -- a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's
   130	  # own. Orca's own installer puts a shim dir on PATH only in Orca
   131	  # terminals, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path that goes
   132	  # stale on the next bump.
   133	  #
   134	  # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: the Orca binary for `orca-ide open` and `serve` to
   135	  # launch; under plain node there is no other, and without it `open` fails
   136	  # and `serve` refuses to start. NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as
   137	  # ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS and cleared, as upstream's shim does.
   138	  # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
   139	  orcaCli = pkgs.runCommand "orca-cli-${version}" {
   140	    pname = "orca-cli";
   141	    inherit version;
   142	    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
   143	  } ''
   144	    mkdir -p $out/bin
   145	    cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
   146	    #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
   147	    export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE="''${ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app}"
   148	    export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="''${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
   149	    export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="''${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
   150	    unset NODE_OPTIONS NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE
   151	    exec ${pkgs.nodejs_24}/bin/node ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js "$@"
   152	    EOF
   153	    chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide
   154	    ln -s orca-ide $out/bin/orca
   155	  '';
   156	
   157	  # Orca's agent skills, from the repo at the commit this AppImage was built
   158	  # from: `orca skills install` pins `npx skills add` to it, and the bundled
   159	  # resources/skills/current-manifest.json holds their sha256s. Bump this rev
   160	  # with the version — it is the `sourceCommit` in out/main/index.js of
   161	  # app.asar, and the test holds it to that. A fetch in this module rather
   162	  # than a flake input, because the rev tracks `version` above, not the
   163	  # repo's head; `nix flake update` does not touch it. The rev is in the
   164	  # store name so a rev bump without a hash bump fails to fetch instead of
   165	  # reusing the old tree. The skills are stubs that call
   166	  # `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so they need orcaCli above.
   167	  #
   168	  # A subset of the bundled ten: no Jira, no emulator. Each is a read-only
   169	  # store symlink, so Orca's own Settings > Skills "update" (npx skills add)
   170	  # will fail on them or replace them, and home-manager then refuses to
   171	  # clobber; update by bumping here instead.
   172	  orcaSkillsSrc = pkgs.fetchFromGitHub rec {
   173	    name = "orca-skills-${rev}";
   174	    owner = "stablyai";
   175	    repo = "orca";
   176	    rev = "e6f7fba58e8e47b45e4343f99101b3ca9e05a5da";
   177	    hash = "REDACTED";
   178	  };
   179	  orcaSkills = [
   180	    "orca-cli" "orchestration" "computer-use" "orca-per-workspace-env"
   181	    "orca-linear" "linear-tickets"
   182	  ];
   183	
   184	  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
   185	  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
   186	  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
   187	  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
   188	  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own
   189	  # (Ctrl+1..9 tab select, Alt+Z word wrap, Ctrl+PageUp/Down), not a Linux
   190	  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,
   191	  # and the few orcaPinned below puts back on purpose.
   192	  #
   193	  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
   194	  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
   195	  # Chords Hyprland binds would be dead keys, so those actions are unbound --
   196	  # on shiori 19 of them, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,
   197	  # plus Super+B/N/E, the digits, and their Shift forms. orcaPinned below
   198	  # rebinds the ones worth having elsewhere. The build log lists every one.
   199	  #
   200	  # A running Orca reads the file once; after a switch, restart it (or run its
   201	  # keybindings reload) for the new table to apply. Resetting a generated
   202	  # shortcut in Orca's settings re-applies the Mac chord at the next switch:
   203	  # Orca stores a reset, and a pick of its own Linux default, as the same
   204	  # deletion, so neither sticks -- set some other chord, or unbind, instead.
   205	  #
   206	  # Find goes on Ctrl+S, emacs' isearch, everywhere but the terminal; there
   207	  # C-s is the shell's own search, so terminal search is left unbound.
   208	  #
   209	  # Previous/next worktree, in list order, on Alt+Up/Down: the Mac chord,
   210	  # Super+Shift+Up/Down, is Hyprland's. Orca catches it before any widget, so
   211	  # this takes M-<up>/<down> from the terminal and the editor's move-line too,
   212	  # deliberately.
   213	  orcaPinned = {
   214	    "editor.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   215	    "browser.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   216	    "chat.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   217	    "settings.search" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
   218	    "worktree.navigateUp" = [ "Alt+ArrowUp" ];
   219	    "worktree.navigateDown" = [ "Alt+ArrowDown" ];
   220	  };
   221	  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
   222	    lib.concatMap
   223	      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
   224	      # bind, bindl, binde, ...: the lists. `binds` is a config section, a set.
   225	      (builtins.filter (k: lib.hasPrefix "bind" k && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s));
   226	  macKeybindings = pkgs.runCommand "orca-mac-keybindings" {
   227	    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper pkgs.jq ];
   228	  } ''
   229	    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
   230	    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
   231	    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
   232	      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \
   233	      ${pkgs.writeText "orca-pinned.json" (builtins.toJSON orcaPinned)} \
   234	      > $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
   235	    # The merge runs Orca's conflict check on the merged file at activation,
   236	    # so the keybinding module (and its one sibling import) ships alongside.
   237	    mkdir -p $out/lib/shared
   238	    cp -r app/out/shared/keybindings.js app/out/shared/keybindings \
   239	      app/out/shared/tui-agent-display-names.js $out/lib/shared/
   240	    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \
   241	      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
   242	    # One real merge, so an Orca bump that moves an import or an export the
   243	    # merge uses fails here, not as a warning at every activation. The seed
   244	    # is a string (comma-list) value, so the shorthand parser runs too; it
   245	    # sits on a New-agent-tab action, unbound on every platform, so the
   246	    # table never claims it whatever Hyprland binds. The check is that every
   247	    # generated entry landed as generated, and the seed survived.
   248	    mkdir -p $TMPDIR/home/.orca
   249	    echo '{"version":1,"keybindings":{},"platforms":{"linux":{"tab.newAgent.claude":"Alt+F12, Alt+Shift+F12"}}}' \
   250	      > $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json
   251	    HOME=$TMPDIR/home $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings 2> merge.err
   252	    if [ -s merge.err ] \
   253	       || ! jq -e --slurpfile o $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json '
   254	            .platforms.linux as $l
   255	            | ($o[0] | to_entries | all(.value == $l[.key]))
   256	              and $l["tab.newAgent.claude"] == "Alt+F12, Alt+Shift+F12"' \
   257	            $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json >/dev/null \
   258	       || [ ! -s $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json ]; then
   259	      cat merge.err >&2; echo "orca: build-time merge did not apply the table" >&2; exit 1
   260	    fi
   261	  '';
   262	  # ~/.orca/keybindings.json is Orca's read-write state: its settings UI saves
   263	  # into the same platforms.linux section, by atomic rename, so a home.file
   264	  # symlink would be replaced on the first edit. So the generated keys are
   265	  # merged into whatever Orca last wrote, owning only what the last merge
   266	  # wrote (a sidecar records it), and a UI edit outranks them -- the rules
   267	  # are at the top of nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js.
   268	  # tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh.
   269	in
   270	{
   271	  home.packages =
   272	    lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop) [ orcaGui orcaCli ];
   273	
   274	  home.file = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop) (lib.listToAttrs (map (name: {
   275	    name = ".claude/skills/${name}";
   276	    value.source = "${orcaSkillsSrc}/skills/${name}";
   277	  }) orcaSkills));
   278	
   279	  home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop)
   280	    (lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" ] ''
   281	      $DRY_RUN_CMD ${macKeybindings}/bin/orca-mac-keybindings
   282	    '');
   283	}
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
     3	# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
     4	# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
     5	# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
     6	#
     7	# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
     8	# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
     9	# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
    10	# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
    11	# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
    12	# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
    13	# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
    14	# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
    15	# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
    16	# held to.
    17	#
    18	# Usage:
    19	#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
    20	
    21	set -u
    22	set -o pipefail
    23	
    24	fails=0; n=0
    25	pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
    26	fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
    27	T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
    28	
    29	FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
    30	# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
    31	# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
    32	HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
    33	SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
    34	
    35	pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
    36	  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
    37	    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
    38	}
    39	drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
    40	want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
    41	  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
    42	CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
    43	gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
    44	GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
    45	echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
    46	
    47	# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
    48	# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
    49	# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
    50	for b in orca orca-ide; do
    51	  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
    52	  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
    53	done
    54	if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
    55	  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
    56	else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
    57	
    58	# No sandbox between the caller and the CLI: a plain exec of node, so
    59	# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.
    60	if grep -q 'exec .*/bin/node ' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" && ! grep -q bwrap "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
    61	  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
    62	else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
    63	
    64	# Under plain node, `orca-ide open` has no Orca binary to spawn but
    65	# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).
    66	# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too,
    67	# minus nixGL.
    68	app=$(sed -nE 's|.*ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-([^}]*)\}.*|\1|p' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")
    69	if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
    70	  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
    71	else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
    72	
    73	# The GUI wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with its
    74	# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
    75	# wayland first (Hyprland has no X server, and Orca's gate picks X11 without
    76	# it), except in node mode or when the caller sets a platform itself --
    77	# `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`. A bare `--ozone-platform x11`
    78	# does not count: Chromium takes no switch value from the next word, so
    79	# Orca's display gate sees an empty one and falls back to X11; nor does a
    80	# -hint, which the gate ignores.
    81	inner=$(grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*/bin/orca-ide-app' "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" | tail -1)
    82	[ -n "$inner" ] || inner="$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"  # no nixGL layer
    83	sed -E 's|^exec .*/\.orca-ide-unwrapped "\$@"$|printf "%s\\n" "$@"|' "$inner" > "$T/argv"
    84	grep -q '^printf' "$T/argv" && ! grep -q 'orca-ide-unwrapped' "$T/argv" \
    85	  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }
    86	argv() { env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE bash "$T/argv" "$@" | paste -sd' '; }
    87	for c in "open|--ozone-platform=wayland open" \
    88	         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
    89	         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform x11" \
    90	         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
    91	         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do
    92	  in=${c%%|*}; want=${c#*|}
    93	  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    94	  got=$(argv $in)
    95	  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "GUI argv: '$in' -> '$want'"
    96	  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi
    97	done
    98	got=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 bash "$T/argv" -e 1 | paste -sd' ')
    99	if [ "$got" = "-e 1" ]; then pass "GUI argv: node mode gets no flag"
   100	else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi
   101	
   102	# And for real: the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
   103	# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
   104	# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
   105	# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
   106	# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits at Orca's gate instead.
   107	nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
   108	ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"
   109	node_ok=
   110	if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
   111	  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
   112	else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
   113	
   114	# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
   115	# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
   116	# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
   117	# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
   118	# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
   119	if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
   120	  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
   121	else
   122	ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
   123	  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
   124	  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
   125	for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
   126	if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
   127	else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
   128	fi
   129	
   130	# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
   131	# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
   132	contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
   133	  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
   134	[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
   135	manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
   136	
   137	# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
   138	# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
   139	# completion too.
   140	clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
   141	outside() {
   142	  local u=() v
   143	  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
   144	  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
   145	}
   146	
   147	got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
   148	if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
   149	else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
   150	
   151	# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
   152	for b in orca-ide orca; do
   153	  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
   154	  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
   155	  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
   156	done
   157	
   158	# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
   159	outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
   160	if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
   161	else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
   162	
   163	# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
   164	rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
   165	if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
   166	  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
   167	else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
   168	
   169	for s in $SKILLS; do
   170	  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
   171	    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }

# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

## NO EMAILS

**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages,
docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts.
This repo is public, and an address is a durable identifier that spreads: it
leaks the work/personal boundary, it enumerates people, and once written it gets
copied onward.

Refer to an account by its **role** — "the personal Google account", "the work
account", "the project's GCS service agent" — or record the command that
recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather
than pasting its output. Role-based wording is better documentation anyway: "must
be the personal account, not the work one" survives an address change; a pasted
address does not.

If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first.

The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`, which git
requires and which is on every commit regardless.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a diverged checkout — **both refusals are
the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route around them
with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass `--local`
deliberately and say that you did.

A checkout on master that is strictly behind `origin/master` fast-forwards to
the fetched SHA and continues — no refusal, nothing to decide.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

index 00000000..6c3580d6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# No sandbox between the caller and the CLI: a plain exec of node, so
+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.
+if grep -q 'exec .*/bin/node ' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" && ! grep -q bwrap "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
+
+# Under plain node, `orca-ide open` has no Orca binary to spawn but
+# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).
+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too,
+# minus nixGL.
+app=$(sed -nE 's|.*ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-([^}]*)\}.*|\1|p' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")
+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# The GUI wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with its
+# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
+# wayland first (Hyprland has no X server, and Orca's gate picks X11 without
+# it), except in node mode or when the caller sets a platform itself --
+# `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`. A bare `--ozone-platform x11`
+# does not count: Chromium takes no switch value from the next word, so
+# Orca's display gate sees an empty one and falls back to X11; nor does a
+# -hint, which the gate ignores.
+inner=$(grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*/bin/orca-ide-app' "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" | tail -1)
+[ -n "$inner" ] || inner="$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"  # no nixGL layer
+sed -E 's|^exec .*/\.orca-ide-unwrapped "\$@"$|printf "%s\\n" "$@"|' "$inner" > "$T/argv"
+grep -q '^printf' "$T/argv" && ! grep -q 'orca-ide-unwrapped' "$T/argv" \
+  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }
+argv() { env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE bash "$T/argv" "$@" | paste -sd' '; }
+for c in "open|--ozone-platform=wayland open" \
+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
+         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do
+  in=${c%%|*}; want=${c#*|}
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+  got=$(argv $in)
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "GUI argv: '$in' -> '$want'"
+  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi
+done
+got=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 bash "$T/argv" -e 1 | paste -sd' ')
+if [ "$got" = "-e 1" ]; then pass "GUI argv: node mode gets no flag"
+else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi
+
+# And for real: the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
+# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
+# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
+# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
+# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits at Orca's gate instead.
+nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"
+node_ok=
+if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
+  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
+# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
+# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
+# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
+# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
+if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
+  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
+else
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
+fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
+# completion too.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

Contents of /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/orca-cli-node/CLAUDE.md:

## NO EMAILS

**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages,
docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts.
This repo is public, and an address is a durable identifier that spreads: it
leaks the work/personal boundary, it enumerates people, and once written it gets
copied onward.

Refer to an account by its **role** — "the personal Google account", "the work
account", "the project's GCS service agent" — or record the command that
recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather
than pasting its output. Role-based wording is better documentation anyway: "must
be the personal account, not the work one" survives an address change; a pasted
address does not.

If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first.

The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`, which git
requires and which is on every commit regardless.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a diverged checkout — **both refusals are
the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route around them
with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass `--local`
deliberately and say that you did.

A checkout on master that is strictly behind `origin/master` fast-forwards to
the fetched SHA and continues — no refusal, nothing to decide.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

</system-reminder>

# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  eval:
    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        sandbox = true
      # Pinned the same way nix-home.yml pins its attic-client: the image ships
      # no coreutils/grep/jq, and the test scripts in tests/ assume a normal
      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch
      # below. Any host with a full desktop config will do.
      TEST_HOST: utsuho
    steps:
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      # Do NOT echo $FORGE_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: authorise git against the private input
        env:
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".username oauth2
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".helper \
            '!f() { test "$1" = get && printf "password=%s\n" "$FORGE_TOKEN"; }; f'

      # The whole contract with `hmeval` is this file plus the two markers
      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".
      - name: run the request
        env:
          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu

          req=.hmeval-request
          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
            case "$k" in
              mode)  mode=$v ;;
              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
              tests) tests=$v ;;
              attr)  attr=$v ;;
            esac
          done < "$req"

          echo "hmeval: mode=$mode"
          echo "---8<--- hmeval"
          rc=0

          # $hosts and $tests are unquoted in the loops below ON PURPOSE: they
          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.
          # Quoting them turns the whole list into one argument, which fails as
          # "attribute 'utsuho fujiwara ...' missing" rather than as a syntax
          # error, so it looks like a broken flake instead of a broken quote.
          # hmeval guarantees they contain no other whitespace.

          case "$mode" in
            eval)
              # --no-link/--raw keeps this to evaluation plus whatever IFD the
              # config genuinely needs; nothing is pushed anywhere.
              for h in $hosts; do
                if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#homeConfigurations.$h.activationPackage.drvPath"); then
                  printf '  %-10s %s\n' "$h" "$out"
                else
                  printf '  %-10s FAILED\n' "$h"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            attr)
              if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#$attr"); then
                printf '  %s\n' "$out"
              else
                printf '  FAILED: .#%s\n' "$attr"
                rc=1
              fi
              ;;
            tests)
              # Several scripts in tests/ build the thing they test by way of
              # `homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname)` — fine on a box that
              # is one of the hosts, useless in a container whose hostname is
              # its own ID. Run 137 died twice over with
              #
              #   does not provide attribute
              #   'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4.config.home.packages'
              #
              # Rather than teach eight scripts a new seam, tell the ephemeral
              # container it is a host. It only ever needs to be *a* host whose
              # config contains the script under test; utsuho has all of them.
              printf '%s' "$TEST_HOST" > /etc/hostname
              echo "  (as $TEST_HOST)"

              # tests/*.sh are ordinary shell: they want coreutils, grep, sed
              # and jq, none of which the nix image has. Run them inside a
              # pinned shell rather than teaching each script to cope.
              tools="github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$TOOLS_REV"
              for t in $tests; do
                echo "  === $t"
                if nix shell \
                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
                     -c bash "$t"; then
                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
                else
                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            *)
              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
              rc=1
              ;;
          esac

          echo "---8<--- end"
          exit $rc
29:  GOPATH = "${home}/devel/go";
31:  # Prepend the home-manager profile bin so it lands in environment.d too. Login
