# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  eval:
    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        sandbox = true
      # Pinned the same way nix-home.yml pins its attic-client: the image ships
      # no coreutils/grep/jq, and the test scripts in tests/ assume a normal
      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch
      # below. Any host with a full desktop config will do.
      TEST_HOST: utsuho
    steps:
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      # Do NOT echo $FORGE_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: authorise git against the private input
        env:
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".username oauth2
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".helper \
            '!f() { test "$1" = get && printf "password=%s\n" "$FORGE_TOKEN"; }; f'

      # The whole contract with `hmeval` is this file plus the two markers
      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".
      - name: run the request
        env:
          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu

          req=.hmeval-request
          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
            case "$k" in
              mode)  mode=$v ;;
              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
              tests) tests=$v ;;
              attr)  attr=$v ;;
            esac
          done < "$req"

          echo "hmeval: mode=$mode"
          echo "---8<--- hmeval"
          rc=0

          # $hosts and $tests are unquoted in the loops below ON PURPOSE: they
          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.
          # Quoting them turns the whole list into one argument, which fails as
          # "attribute 'utsuho fujiwara ...' missing" rather than as a syntax
          # error, so it looks like a broken flake instead of a broken quote.
          # hmeval guarantees they contain no other whitespace.

          case "$mode" in
            eval)
              # --no-link/--raw keeps this to evaluation plus whatever IFD the
              # config genuinely needs; nothing is pushed anywhere.
              for h in $hosts; do
                if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#homeConfigurations.$h.activationPackage.drvPath"); then
                  printf '  %-10s %s\n' "$h" "$out"
                else
                  printf '  %-10s FAILED\n' "$h"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            attr)
              if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#$attr"); then
                printf '  %s\n' "$out"
              else
                printf '  FAILED: .#%s\n' "$attr"
                rc=1
              fi
              ;;
            tests)
              # Several scripts in tests/ build the thing they test by way of
              # `homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname)` — fine on a box that
              # is one of the hosts, useless in a container whose hostname is
              # its own ID. Run 137 died twice over with
              #
              #   does not provide attribute
              #   'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4.config.home.packages'
              #
              # Rather than teach eight scripts a new seam, tell the ephemeral
              # container it is a host. It only ever needs to be *a* host whose
              # config contains the script under test; utsuho has all of them.
              printf '%s' "$TEST_HOST" > /etc/hostname
              echo "  (as $TEST_HOST)"

              # tests/*.sh are ordinary shell: they want coreutils, grep, sed
              # and jq, none of which the nix image has. Run them inside a
              # pinned shell rather than teaching each script to cope.
              tools="github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$TOOLS_REV"
              for t in $tests; do
                echo "  === $t"
                if nix shell \
                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
                     -c bash "$t"; then
                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
                else
                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            *)
              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
              rc=1
              ;;
          esac

          echo "---8<--- end"
          exit $rc

# Use 'unshare -Ur true' as a heuristic to detect whether user namespaces are available.
# Notes:
#   - When running as root, this check will always succeed even if the sandbox configuration
#     actually relies on unprivileged user namespaces. In practice, Chrome/Electron usually
#     disables or adjusts the sandbox separately when running as root, so this probe is mostly
#     a no-op in that scenario.
#   - On minimal systems (e.g. Alpine or stripped-down containers) 'unshare' may not exist.
#     In that case the shell will return exit code 127 ("command not found"), which will cause
#     us to add '--no-sandbox'. This is an intentional fail-safe: we prefer the app to start
#     without sandboxing rather than crash on startup.
if [ $HAVE_NO_SANDBOX -eq 0 ] && ! unshare -Ur true 2>/dev/null ; then
  NO_SANDBOX=(--no-sandbox)
fi

atexit()
{
  if [ $isEulaAccepted == 1 ] ; then
    if [ $NUMBER_OF_ARGS -eq 0 ] ; then
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}"
    else
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}" "${args[@]}"
    fi
  fi
}

error()
{
  if [ -x /usr/bin/zenity ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --error --text "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  else
    echo "${1}"
  fi
  exit 1
}

yesno()
{
  TITLE=$1
  TEXT=$2
  if [ -x /usr/bin/zenity ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --question --title="$TITLE" --text="$TEXT" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --title "$TITLE" --yesno "$TEXT" || exit 0
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --title "$TITLE" --clear --yesno "$TEXT" 10 80 || exit 0
  else
    echo "zenity, kdialog, Xdialog missing. Skipping ${THIS}."
    exit 0
  fi
}

check_dep()
{
  DEP=$1
  if ! command -v "$DEP" &>/dev/null ; then
    echo "$DEP is missing. Skipping ${THIS}."
    exit 0
  fi
}

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE" ] ; then

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

35:     # `orca-ide open` (orcaCli below) spawns the GUI detached, but every
36:     # wrapper layer execs the next, so this bwrap is the CLI's own child, and
37:     # --die-with-parent SIGKILLs the window the moment `open` returns.
38:     dieWithParent = false;
39:     # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop. Upstream's .deb
40:     # puts the CLI on PATH as `orca-ide` and leaves the GUI off it, and Orca's
41:     # skills tell agents to run `orca-ide` outside an Orca terminal -- so
42:     # `orca-ide` is orcaCli below, and the GUI is `orca-ide-app`, which the
43:     # desktop Exec and meta.mainProgram use. Written by hand, not with
44:     # makeShellWrapper: --add-flags cannot make the flag below conditional.
45:     #
46:     # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
47:     # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
48:     # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
49:     # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
50:     # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
51:     # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
52:     # is a flag on the command line -- except in node mode: the CLI's `serve`
53:     # probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as
54:     # argv, and Node rejects the flag ("bad option", exit 9). Nor when the
55:     # caller sets a platform itself (Electron serve appends
56:     # --ozone-platform=x11): `--ozone-platform=<value>` before any `--`, which
57:     # is what Orca's display gate reads -- a bare `--ozone-platform x11` gives
58:     # Chromium an empty value, and a -hint is only a preference. (The flag
59:     # also counts as explicit to Orca's own serve-mode X11 restart, so a
60:     # hand-run `orca-ide-app --serve` stays on wayland; the CLI's serve
61:     # passes x11 itself.)
62:     #
63:     # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
64:     # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
65:     # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher's bin/orca moves aside
66:     # to .orca-ide-unwrapped -- `orca` is orcaCli's name in the profile, and
67:     # tests/sandbox-fonts.sh finds the launcher by this one -- and
68:     # orca-ide-app execs it, the flag first when due.
69:     extraInstallCommands = ''
70:       mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
71:       cat > $out/bin/orca-ide-app <<'EOF'
72:       #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
73:       explicit=
74:       for a in "$@"; do
75:         case $a in --) break ;; --ozone-platform=?*) explicit=1; break ;; esac
76:       done
77:       if [ -z "$explicit" ] && [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then
78:         set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"
79:       fi
80:       exec ${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped "$@"
81:       EOF
82:       chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide-app
83:       install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
84:         $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
113:   appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };
114: 
115:   # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
116:   # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
117:   # same reason parsec gets it.
118:   orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;
119: 
120:   # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
121:   # Linux) and `orca`. Upstream avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it is
122:   # usually the GNOME screen reader; it is not installed here, so `orca` is
123:   # the CLI too. (Were it installed, the profile comes first on PATH --
124:   # env.nix -- so `orca` would still be this CLI.) The skills say `orca-ide`.
125:   #
126:   # It is plain JavaScript: upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide runs it on the
127:   # bundled Electron in node mode, but nothing in it needs Electron, so it
128:   # runs on nixpkgs' node of the same major (Electron 43 bundles node 24)
129:   # with no sandbox -- a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's
130:   # own. Orca's own installer puts a shim dir on PATH only in Orca
131:   # terminals, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path that goes
132:   # stale on the next bump.
133:   #
134:   # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: the Orca binary for `orca-ide open` and `serve` to
135:   # launch; under plain node there is no other, and without it `open` fails
136:   # and `serve` refuses to start. NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as
137:   # ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS and cleared, as upstream's shim does.
138:   # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
139:   orcaCli = pkgs.runCommand "orca-cli-${version}" {
140:     pname = "orca-cli";
141:     inherit version;
142:     meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
143:   } ''
144:     mkdir -p $out/bin
145:     cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
146:     #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
147:     export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE="''${ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app}"
148:     export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="''${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
149:     export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="''${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
150:     unset NODE_OPTIONS NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

Host-membership lists and package-build smoke tests used to be in here and are
not any more: a drifted host gate shows up the first time you run the tool, and
what a build produced belongs to that derivation's own `installCheckPhase`,
where it gates the build instead of being checked after the fact.

input.message:
Round 4 review of `git diff origin/master..HEAD` (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, tests/sandbox-fonts.sh). I wrote nothing and launched no Orca process. I checked the claims against the bundled 1.4.238 code in /nix/store/k0m448kgqa8i0mhksvz488q9663d0g99-orca-1.4.238-extracted (the packed main code in resources/app.asar, plus out/cli/runtime/*.js and out/shared/headless-serve-ozone-platform.js in resources/app.asar.unpacked), against home-manager's nixgl.nix `makePackageWrapper`, and against env.nix and home.nix.

**Critical**

None.

**Important**

1. The "bare `--ozone-platform x11` falls back to X11" reasoning doesn't match the bundled code, and the test case built on it checks a difference that changes nothing.
   - **Where:** orca.nix:56-58, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:76-80 and the bare-flag case at :88. The round-3 commit message says the same thing.
   - **What the gate does with an empty value:** the comments say Orca's display gate turns an empty value into X11. The gate in app.asar (`dPn`) only accepts `x11` or `wayland` from the switch, or from `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`. Anything else, including an empty value, gives `_Q(DISPLAY) || hPn(env)`: either a live X display or a live Wayland socket will do. It is not "falls back to X11".
   - **Why the prepend does nothing here:** Chromium's CommandLine keeps the last value of a repeated switch. So `--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform x11` still resolves to an empty `ozone-platform`, the same as not prepending at all.
   - **Upstream does it differently:** upstream's own `hasExplicitOzonePlatform` (out/shared/headless-serve-ozone-platform.js) and the serve-restart check `PEn` both count a bare `--ozone-platform` as explicit. Round 2 matched upstream; round 3 moved away from it on this reasoning.
   - **Impact:** behaviour is harmless either way. But the comments explain a mechanism that isn't there, and the test pins an argv that doesn't do what it claims.
   - **Fix:** either say that the bare form is left to Chromium (the prepend is overridden, so it is neither helped nor hurt), or go back to upstream's rule and drop or re-label the bare-flag test case.

**nits**

1. orca.nix:46-48 (an older sentence in a paragraph this diff edits) says "Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise." `dPn` in 1.4.238 accepts either display in that case. The measured exit 1 may come from inside the sandbox (for example `hPn` not finding the socket under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, or Chromium's own platform init), not from the gate picking X11. Worth rewording or re-measuring.
2. orca.nix:55 says "Electron serve appends --ozone-platform=x11". It is the CLI's serve: out/cli/runtime/launch.js:160 does `childArgs.push(...headlessServeOzonePlatformSwitches(...))`. Line 60 already says "the CLI's serve passes x11 itself", so the two should use the same wording.
3. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:49 says "in the profile it would shadow one of them". Two packages both providing bin/orca-ide in home.packages fail as a buildEnv collision; they don't shadow each other. Say "collide".
4. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:103-109 (`nodisplay`) unsets WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY but not WAYLAND_SOCKET. `hPn` treats a numeric WAYLAND_SOCKET as a live Wayland display, so the "exits at Orca's gate" guarantee depends on it being unset too. It is rarely set in a shell, but adding `-u WAYLAND_SOCKET` makes the guarantee complete.
5. home.nix:275 and :3056 list the `config.lib.nixGL.wrap` users as "ghostty, hyprlock, hyprpaper". orca (now `orcaGui`, orca.nix:118) and parsec are missing. This was already incomplete on master; touch it only if you want the list accurate.
6. README.md:107-128 doesn't list tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, though tests/sandbox-fonts.sh is listed. The list is curated (32 of 43 scripts), so this is optional.

**Verified correct**

- **PATH comment (orca.nix:123-124):** env.nix:35 puts `~/.nix-profile/bin` before `$PATH`, as stated.
- **nixGL wrap and the test's `inner` lookup:**
  - `makePackageWrapper` writes one `makeWrapper ... --add-flags "$file"` per `bin/*`, so `grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*/bin/orca-ide-app' | tail -1` (test :81) finds the inner script.
  - The `bin/*` glob skips dotfiles, so `.orca-ide-unwrapped` stays a plain symlink and isn't wrapped.
  - The name is kept, so pname "orca" still matches in `pkg_attr`.
  - The sandbox-fonts regex `.*orca-[0-9.]+` doesn't match `orca-cli-1.4.238`, so it still picks the GUI.
- **orca.nix:134-137 and the CLI wrapper:**
  - `resolveForegroundOrcaExecutable` throws without ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE or `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, and `launchOrcaApp` throws the same way.
  - `spawnDetached` uses `detached: true`, so the dieWithParent reasoning at orca.nix:35-37 holds.
  - The NODE_OPTIONS / NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE handling matches upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide line for line.
- **orca.nix:59-61:** `PEn` counts the flag as explicit, so a hand-run `--serve` isn't re-executed onto X11.
- **Each test case goes red if its claim regresses:**
  - argv cases: removing the prepend, the `=?*` explicit check (for x11 and for -hint), the `--` break, or the node-mode check each fails a case.
  - The node-mode probe fails with exit 9 if the flag leaks into node mode.
  - The lifetime case: with dieWithParent on, the parent (bash -c or the exec'd `sleep 4`) exits at 4s, before the 6s marker is written.
- **Process cleanup:** no path leaves Orca running or opens a window, as long as nothing strips ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE before Electron starts.
  - Every real launch has ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and no display. The lifetime child exits itself at 7s, and the lifetime case runs only when node mode works.
  - No CLI command that opens Orca is run. The CLI calls run under `outside` (ORCA_* unset), so ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE falls back to the default and nothing reaches a running Orca.
  - An interrupted run leaves at most the self-exiting 7s node process.
- **Secrets:** nothing prints environment values. No `set -x`. Failure messages carry only CLI output, the node probe's stdout and last stderr line, argv echoes, and store paths. ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN does reach the two GUI probes' environment (they don't run under `outside`), but it is never printed.
- **CI (.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml):** every tool the test uses (coreutils incl. timeout/seq/paste/sha256sum, gnugrep, gnused, jq, bash, nix-store) is in the pinned `nix shell`. /etc/hostname is written as utsuho. As root, AppRun's `unshare -Ur` check passes, so it adds no `--no-sandbox` in node mode. The GUI probes still need bwrap to work in the privileged container, which tests/sandbox-fonts.sh already needs.
- **Shell and Nix mechanics:**
  - The Nix `''` strings strip indentation so the heredoc's EOF lands at column 0.
  - `''${...}` escapes are correct, and `placeholder "out"` is right inside extraInstallCommands.
